lesson.subtitle: Lesson 6 -- Review: Must, Should, Can
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Fábia | Lesson 6 -- Review: Must, Should, Can

listenings.text: Fabia, this is David. A quick reminder before Thursday. Head office needs the audit trail for the last two years. We must have it before the call. You should also send the confidentiality agreement. And if you can, add the name of the partner who signs it. Nothing else for now. Thank you.

Fabia, this is Karen. Here is the good version of that answer, the one that works. Four people can see the data. Everyone must sign a confidentiality agreement. In a breach, we must notify you within twenty-four hours. That is regulatory. We can give your auditors read-only access. You should keep a copy on your side too.

matching.title: The four words again
defs: the record of who changed what, and when
when data gets out and it should not have
required by the law, not by the company
the promise that you do not share what you see

items.situation: "Who can see our data?" One sentence, with the number.
tips: Four people can see the data.

items.situation: "What happens in a breach?" One sentence, with must.
tips: We must notify you within twenty-four hours.

items.situation: "Can our auditors have access?" One sentence, with can.
tips: Yes, we can give them read-only access.

items.situation: Recommend something. One sentence, with should.
tips: You should keep a copy on your side.

items.situation: Ask head office for the file. One question, with could.
tips: Could you send us the file by Friday?

arguebank.label: Useful language
items: A says must. B says we would try to.
A gives a number. B does not.
"We must" is a rule, not a promise.
"We would try to" sounds like a maybe.
That is regulatory, not our policy.
I would rather sound firm than polite.
The second one is not kinder, it is weaker.
